The corpus gives only partial text on this, so I can confirm the key-facts-statement and digital-disclosure rules but not the full penal-charge disclosure wording.

- **Key Facts Statement (para 29, RBI NBFC Responsible Business Conduct Directions 2025):** For retail and MSME term loans sanctioned on or after 1 October 2024, the NBFC must give a KFS to every prospective borrower before the loan contract is executed, in the standard format in Annex I and in a language the borrower understands. The KFS must be explained, and the borrower must acknowledge understanding. It must carry a unique proposal number and remain valid for at least three working days (one working day for tenors under seven days). It must include an APR computation (covering all charges) and the full amortisation schedule.
- **Penal charges (para 30):** The excerpts I could see confirm that penalties for default may be levied only for non-compliance with material loan terms, and that the Board-approved penal charge policy must keep in mind that the purpose of penal charges is to deter default, not to generate income. The disclosure requirements in the full text of para 30 (including any website or loan-agreement items) could not be retrieved, because the passage fetches were refused as duplicates.
- **Digital loans (Credit Facilities Directions 2025, para 9):** The NBFC must provide the KFS, and penal charges follow the Responsible Business Conduct Directions. Digitally signed KFS, sanction letter and terms must flow automatically to the borrower's verified email or SMS on execution. The NBFC's website must carry its digital lending products, grievance mechanism and related details in a prominent place.
- **Annex I:** Part 1 of the KFS format covers interest, fees and charges, and Part 2 covers the loan-agreement clauses on recovery agents and grievance redressal. I could not read the full Annex, so I cannot confirm whether it has a specific line for penal charges or missed-EMI consequences.

I could not confirm from the corpus what the loan agreement must say about penal charges or missed-EMI consequences, or the exact website disclosure items for penal charges. Those need the full text of para 30 and Annex I.

data.content: No. Under para 30 of the NBFC Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025, penalty for a missed EMI (default) must be levied only as "penal charges," not as "penal interest" added to the rate of interest, and the NBFC may not introduce any additional component to the rate of interest. Penal charges also cannot be capitalised, so no further interest is computed on them, though the NBFC may charge interest on unpaid EMI at the contracted rate until remediation. This applies to fresh loans from April 1, 2024, with existing loans switched over by June 30, 2024, and it excludes credit cards, ECBs, trade credits, structured obligations and other foreign currency loans.

30. An NBFC shall adhere to the following instructions in respect of all the fresh loans
availed from April 1, 2024 onwards. In case of existing loans, the switchover to new
penal charges regime shall be applicable from June 30, 2024. These instructions
shall be applicable to all credit facilities offered by the NBFC but shall not apply to
credit cards, external commercial borrowings, trade credits (rupee / foreign
currency export credit) and structured obligations which are covered under product
specific directions, as also other foreign currency loans.
(1) Penalty, if charged, for non-compliance of material terms and conditions of loan
contract by the borrower shall be treated as ‘penal charges’ and shall not be levied
in the form of ‘penal interest’ that is added to the rate of interest charged on the
advances. There shall be no capitalisation of penal charges, i.e., no further interest
computed on such charges. However, this will not affect the normal procedures for
compounding of interest in the loan account. Therefore, the NBFC may charge
interest on unpaid interest (including on unpaid EMI) at the contracted rate of
interest till the date of remediation, and not at the penal rate of interest.
Notes:
(i) The material terms and conditions shall be defined, if not already done, as
per the credit policy of the NBFC and they may vary from one category of
loan to another, and also, from lender to lender based on their own
assessment.

mechanism.

Reserve Bank.

30. An NBFC shall adhere to the following instructions in respect of all the fresh loans
(ii) Default in repayment by the borrower is also a type of non-compliance of
material terms and conditions of loan repayment contract by the borrower
and penalty, if charged, for such default shall only be levied in the form of
penal charges and not penal interest. Such penal charges shall be
reasonable and levied by the lenders only on the amount under default in a
non-discriminatory manner as per their Board approved policy. Further, it
shall be ensured that there is no capitalization of the penal charges i.e., no
further interest computed on such charges.
(iii) Additional / fresh penal charges shall not be levied on the earlier outstanding
amount of penal charges.
(iv) An NBFC shall follow the instructions and clarifications, if any, issued by
Central Board of Indirect Taxes & Customs (CBIC) with regard to applicability
of GST on penal charges.
(2) The NBFC shall not introduce any additional component to the rate of interest
and ensure compliance to these guidelines in both letter and spirit.
(3) The NBFC shall formulate a Board approved policy on penal charges or similar
charges on loans, by whatever name called.
(4) The quantum of penal charges shall be reasonable and commensurate with the
non-compliance of material terms and conditions of loan contract without being
discriminatory within a particular loan / product category.
Notes:
(i) Penal charges can be different within the same product category depending
upon the amount of loan and the NBFC may adopt a suitable structure of
penal charges subject to adherence to the above stipulations. The structure
of penal charges within a particular loan / product category shall have to be
uniform irrespective of the constitution of the borrower.

29. The following instructions shall be applicable in case of all new retail and MSME
term loans sanctioned on or after October 1, 2024, including fresh loans to existing
customers, by an NBFC. Credit card receivables are exempted from the provisions
given below:
(1) An NBFC shall provide a KFS to all prospective borrowers to help them take an
informed view before executing the loan contract, as per the standardised format
given in the Annex I. The KFS shall be written in a language understood by such
borrowers. Contents of KFS shall be explained to the borrower and an
acknowledgement shall be obtained that they have understood the same.
(2) The KFS shall be provided with a unique proposal number and shall have a
validity period of at least three working days for loans having tenor of seven days
or more, and a validity period of one working day for loans having tenor of less than
seven days.
Explanation: Validity period refers to the period available to the borrower, after being
provided the KFS by the NBFC, to agree to the terms of the loan. The NBFC shall
be bound by the terms of the loan indicated in the KFS, if agreed to by the borrower
during the validity period.
